problem: VLN work lacks a way to measure an agent's navigational (memory-exploiting) ability, relies on simulator-collected data that may not reflect real-world data, and uses one-shot evaluation that does not match how real robots operate over repeated episodes in the same environment.
motivation: Robots need to follow human language in real environments, but VLN progress is measured in simulators with episodic, memoryless evaluation. Understanding how simulated data differs from real data, and testing whether agents exploit long-term environment consistency, is needed for transfer to real robots.
key_idea: Build a suite of navigation-analysis experiments with new exploitation metrics, a real-world human-dialog robot dataset (RobotSLANG), and an iterative VLN-CE paradigm (I-VLN-CE) where agents must remember and reuse environment knowledge across instructions.
insight: Based only on the abstract: data collected on real robots differs fundamentally from simulator-driven data collection, and agents should be evaluated on how they exploit previously seen regions rather than on isolated episodes. No ablations are available from the abstract.
method: Navigation analysis suite: open-source experiments measuring an agent's ability to exploit information in previously seen regions, with new exploitation metrics
RobotSLANG benchmark: real-world dataset of human-generated dialog for robotic control, as an alternative to simulator-driven data collection
Localization from Dialog History (LDH): task of localizing the robot from dialog history
Navigation from Dialog History (NDH): task of navigating from dialog history using RobotSLANG data
I-VLN-CE: Iterative VLN in Continuous Environments, a training and evaluation paradigm that encourages long-term memory of environment consistencies
